hints: Focus on what the carbon bearing the OH group is attached to, that decides primary, secondary or tertiary.
Reduction of $(CH_3)_2CHCO_2H$ with $LiAlH_4$ gives $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH$, so check how many carbons are joined to the $CH_2OH$ carbon.
Hydrolysis of $CH_3CO_2CH(CH_3)_2$ splits the ester to give back the alcohol from the $OCH(CH_3)_2$ part, so count the carbons on that OH carbon to finish the pair.
walkthrough:
**Find alcohol P from reduction**

Think of $LiAlH_4$ as turning the carboxylic acid group into a $CH_2OH$ group. The rest of the molecule stays the same.

$$ (CH_3)_2CHCO_2H \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} (CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH $$

**Classify alcohol P**

In $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH$, the OH is on a $CH_2$ group. That carbon is joined to only one other carbon atom.

That is the definition of a primary alcohol, so P is primary.

**Find alcohol Q from ester hydrolysis**

Hydrolysis of an ester breaks it into carboxylic acid plus alcohol. The acid comes from the $CH_3CO$ part, the alcohol comes from the $OCH(CH_3)_2$ part.

$$ CH_3CO_2CH(CH_3)_2 + H_2O \rightarrow CH_3CO_2H + HOCH(CH_3)_2 $$

**Classify alcohol Q**

Alcohol Q is $HOCH(CH_3)_2$, which is propan-2-ol. The OH carbon is joined directly to two other carbons.

That is the definition of a secondary alcohol, so Q is secondary. P primary and Q secondary matches one row.

options.A: Incorrect because Q is not primary. $HOCH(CH_3)_2$ has the OH carbon bonded to two methyl carbons, so it is secondary, not primary.
options.B: Correct. P is $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2OH$ where the $CH_2OH$ carbon is bonded to one carbon, so primary. Q is $HOCH(CH_3)_2$ where the $CHOH$ carbon is bonded to two carbons, so secondary.
options.C: Incorrect and reversed. Students choose this if they think reduction keeps the branching at the OH carbon for P, or confuse which side of the ester gives the alcohol for Q.
options.D: Incorrect because P is not secondary. Although the starting acid $(CH_3)_2CHCO_2H$ looks branched, reduction adds a $CH_2$ group so the OH ends up on a $CH_2$ bonded to only one carbon.
